note: Library modules named in no ledger, each with the reason it needs none. Written by scripts/check_module_graded.py --write; reasons are edited by hand. UNREVIEWED means the module was inherited when the check was introduced and nobody has yet decided whether it is a support layer or a missing row.

modules.AISafetyAtlas.Composition.Observability: Perfect monitoring is an observability property of the hazard: a sound and complete monitor exists exactly when the hazard is observation-determined, which is Mathlib's `Function.FactorsThrough` at the membership predicate. Native atlas module, graded through `docs/provenance/compositional-boundaries.md` (LAND-OBS-001), which positions it as mechanization and a safety-facing interface rather than mathematical priority. No printed source states it, so no registry row is required.
modules.AISafetyAtlas.Composition.Rectangularity: A global safe set is independently expressible exactly when it is a product of per-agent local sets, and the strongest independent contracts are its coordinate projections. Native atlas module, graded through `docs/provenance/compositional-boundaries.md` (LAND-COMP-001), which positions it as mechanization and a safety-facing interface rather than mathematical priority. No printed source states it, so no registry row is required.
modules.AISafetyAtlas.Compositional.LocalContrac: Boundary module: it records what local contracts cannot express (agreement is not a rectangle) rather than reproducing a printed result. The literature it cites -- Clarkson-Schneider hyperproperties, communication-complexity rectangles -- is graded through the Compositional.Hyperproperties rows it sits beneath.

modules.AISafetyAtlas.Conjectures.Checks: Verification file, not a result: zero public declarations, not on the atlas root import. It holds every Lean name conjectures.yaml records to the type its row claims, so it is a check on a ledger rather than something a ledger grades.
